### kernel: mm/huge_memory: fix dereferencing invalid pmd migration entry
[CVE-2025-37958](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-37958)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/huge_memory: fix dereferencing invalid pmd migration entry

When migrating a THP, concurrent access to the PMD migration entry during
a deferred split scan can lead to an invalid address access, as
illustrated below.  To prevent this invalid access, it is necessary to
check the PMD migration entry and return early.  In this context, there is
no need to use pmd_to_swp_entry and pfn_swap_entry_to_page to verify the
equality of the target folio.  Since the PMD migration entry is locked, it
cannot be served as the target.

Mailing list discussion and explanation from Hugh Dickins: "An anon_vma
lookup points to a location which may contain the folio of interest, but
might instead contain another folio: and weeding out those other folios is
precisely what the "folio != pmd_folio((*pmd)" check (and the "risk of
replacing the wrong folio" comment a few lines above it) is for."

### kernel: RDMA/mlx5: Fix page_size variable overflow
[CVE-2025-22091](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-22091)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

RDMA/mlx5: Fix page_size variable overflow

Change all variables storing mlx5_umem_mkc_find_best_pgsz() result to
unsigned long to support values larger than 31 and avoid overflow.

For example: If we try to register 4GB of memory that is contiguous in
physical memory, the driver will optimize the page_size and try to use
an mkey with 4GB entity size. The 'unsigned int' page_size variable will
overflow to '0' and we'll hit the WARN_ON() in alloc_cacheable_mr().

### kernel: media: uvcvideo: Fix double free in error path
[CVE-2024-57980](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2024-57980)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

media: uvcvideo: Fix double free in error path

If the uvc_status_init() function fails to allocate the int_urb, it will
free the dev->status pointer but doesn't reset the pointer to NULL. This
results in the kfree() call in uvc_status_cleanup() trying to
double-free the memory. Fix it by resetting the dev->status pointer to
NULL after freeing it.

Reviewed by: Ricardo Ribalda <ribalda@chromium.org>

#### Severity
Moderate

#### References
- [https://access.redhat.com/security/cve/CVE-2024-57980](https://access.redhat.com/security/cve/CVE-2024-57980)

This pull request introduces a new unified LLM model configuration for artifact generation, improves structured output handling, and updates formatting and logging for better clarity and functionality. Key changes include adding support for selecting LLM models dynamically, removing redundant methods, and enhancing artifact generation logic.

### LLM Model Configuration and Artifact Generation Updates:
* Added a new `ARTIFACT_MODEL` configuration in `services/agent_worker/config.py` to dynamically select the model for artifact generation (e.g., "claude", "gemini") (`[services/agent_worker/config.pyR33-R38](diffhunk://#diff-ee2aa9d087b19d7db924e19ee1c2925ad9cd71b3f5a1a587483d1c0ff4ec391cR33-R38)`).
* Updated `create_artifact.py` to use the `ARTIFACT_MODEL` configuration, dynamically determine the structure model, and log the selected model during artifact creation (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-0e81b547fe6253df93eb4426a3c27817601f65fd5e10dbdef1677cfa6035c915L14-R14)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-0e81b547fe6253df93eb4426a3c27817601f65fd5e10dbdef1677cfa6035c915L369-R373)`, `[[3]](diffhunk://#diff-0e81b547fe6253df93eb4426a3c27817601f65fd5e10dbdef1677cfa6035c915L598-R621)`, `[[4]](diffhunk://#diff-0e81b547fe6253df93eb4426a3c27817601f65fd5e10dbdef1677cfa6035c915R664)`, `[[5]](diffhunk://#diff-0e81b547fe6253df93eb4426a3c27817601f65fd5e10dbdef1677cfa6035c915R674-R687)`).

### Unified Structured Output Handling:
* Introduced a new `async_structure` method in `llm_interface.py` to unify structured output generation for both Gemini and Anthropic models, replacing the need for separate methods (`[services/agent_worker/llms/llm_interface.pyR465-R629](diffhunk://#diff-4d1cabad91155de2ee5325b1dd82ffb6b551b4347ac5f63233a2700572ad1a04R465-R629)`).
* Removed the now redundant `async_structure_with_anthropic` and `call_morph_fast_apply` methods to simplify the codebase (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-4d1cabad91155de2ee5325b1dd82ffb6b551b4347ac5f63233a2700572ad1a04L249-L302)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-4d1cabad91155de2ee5325b1dd82ffb6b551b4347ac5f63233a2700572ad1a04L503-R451)`).

### Prompt and Formatting Enhancements:
* Updated artifact generation prompts in `create_artifact.py` to enforce stricter reference formatting and improve financial modeling best practices (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-0e81b547fe6253df93eb4426a3c27817601f65fd5e10dbdef1677cfa6035c915R45-R54)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-0e81b547fe6253df93eb4426a3c27817601f65fd5e10dbdef1677cfa6035c915L95-R96)`).
* Changed the font color for "hardcoded" input values in `formatting.yaml` from black to blue for better visual distinction (`[services/agent_worker/lib/formatting.yamlL39-R39](diffhunk://#diff-2c0e1983c902aaa9a005537013bafd100bd17b8224c2057ec305d9a9630d68b3L39-R39)`).

These changes collectively improve the flexibility, maintainability, and usability of the artifact generation process.

body:
## 🤖 Installing Claude Code GitHub App

This PR adds a GitHub Actions workflow that enables Claude Code integration in our repository.

### What is Claude Code?

[Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code) is an AI coding agent that can help with:
- Bug fixes and improvements  
- Documentation updates
- Implementing new features
- Code reviews and suggestions
- Writing tests
- And more!

### How it works

Once this PR is merged, we'll be able to interact with Claude by mentioning @claude in a pull request or issue comment.
Once the workflow is triggered, Claude will analyze the comment and surrounding context, and execute on the request in a GitHub action.

### Important Notes

- **This workflow won't take effect until this PR is merged**
- **@claude mentions won't work until after the merge is complete**
- The workflow runs automatically whenever Claude is mentioned in PR or issue comments
- Claude gets access to the entire PR or issue context including files, diffs, and previous comments

### Security

- Our Anthropic API key is securely stored as a GitHub Actions secret
- Only users with write access to the repository can trigger the workflow
- All Claude runs are stored in the GitHub Actions run history
- Claude's default tools are limited to reading/writing files and interacting with our repo by creating comments, branches, and commits.
- We can add more allowed tools by adding them to the workflow file like:

```
allowed_tools: Bash(npm install),Bash(npm run build),Bash(npm run lint),Bash(npm run test)
```

There's more information in the [Claude Code action repo](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action).

After merging this PR, let's try mentioning @claude in a comment on any PR to get started!

author: mirinodev
body:
## Summary

Add support for creating tmux sessions with multiple panes (3, 4, 5, 6+ splits) instead of just 2-pane splits, as requested in Issue #154.

## Changes

### New Features
- **`--tmux-h-panes <number>`**: Create specified number of horizontal tmux panes
- **`--tmux-v-panes <number>`**: Create specified number of vertical tmux panes  
- **`--tmux-layout <type>`**: Apply tmux layout (even-horizontal, even-vertical, main-horizontal, main-vertical, tiled)

### Technical Implementation
- Extended `CreateOptions` type with multi-pane support fields
- Enhanced tmux split logic with loop-based pane creation
- Added automatic layout application for optimal space usage
- Maintained backward compatibility with existing 2-pane options
- Proper shell environment inheritance across all panes

### Documentation
- Updated README files (English and Japanese)
- Enhanced command documentation with practical examples
- Added comprehensive usage patterns for development workflows

## Usage Examples

```bash
# Create 3 horizontal panes for microservice development
mst create feature/api --tmux-h-panes 3

# Create 4 vertical panes with main-vertical layout
mst create feature/ui --tmux-v-panes 4 --tmux-layout main-vertical

# Grid layout for complex development environment
mst create feature/dashboard --tmux-h-panes 4 --tmux-layout tiled
```

## Test Plan

- [x] Unit tests for multi-pane creation logic
- [x] Layout application tests for all supported types
- [x] Inside/outside tmux behavior validation
- [x] Error handling and graceful degradation
- [x] Backward compatibility with existing options
- [x] Documentation accuracy and completeness

## Backward Compatibility

✅ Fully backward compatible - existing `--tmux-h` and `--tmux-v` options work unchanged.

Closes #154

bf16由于类型支持问题，在print的时候需要转成fp32，以使用numpy的功能。

- `src/app/messages/page.js` → `src/app/messages/page.tsx`

author: fw-bot
body:
Tour "test_chatbot_clear_answers_on_step_type_change" could fail with following error before this commit:

```
Tour finished with a dirty form view being open.

Dirty form views are automatically saved when the page is closed,
which leads to stray network requests and inconsistencies.
```

The tour was saving the changes to form view but was not awaiting a trigger when the form is saved, thus the tour could end and still see form is dirty.

This commit replaces `.o_form_view` to `.o_form_saved` for awaiting the form is fully saved and not dirty at end of test tour.

Fixes runbot error 230296

author: copilot
body:
This PR implements a complete Ruby 3 Rack service that receives webmentions and creates GitHub pull requests with timestamped branch names, using direct GitHub API calls instead of external dependencies.

## Key Features

### Core Webmention Service
- **Rack-based web service** listening for POST requests on `/webmention`
- **Parameter validation** requiring both `source` and `target` parameters
- **Direct GitHub API integration** using Net::HTTP with proper authentication
- **Timestamped branch names** using format `YYYY-MM-DDTHH-MM-SS-new-webmention`

### Direct GitHub API Implementation
- Creates PRs with title format: "New Webmention Received at {timestamp}"
- PR body contains the webmention data:
  ```
  source: <source from webmention>
  target: <target from webmention>
  ```
- Uses timestamped branch configuration: `head='{timestamp}-new-webmention'`, `base='main'`
- **No external dependencies** - uses only Ruby standard library Net::HTTP
- Supports custom GitHub API endpoints via environment variable

### Configuration & Security
- **Environment variables support**:
  - `WEBMENTION_FORWARDER_REPO` (required): Repository in "owner/repo" format
  - `GITHUB_CREDENTIALS_PATH` (optional): Custom path to GitHub token file (defaults to `~/.github_credentials`)
  - `GITHUB_API_URL` (optional): Custom GitHub API endpoint (defaults to `https://api.github.com`)
- **GitHub Personal Access Token** authentication from file system
- **Comprehensive error handling** with helpful log messages for all failure scenarios

### Testing & CI/CD
- **Comprehensive test suite** with 14 RSpec test cases covering all scenarios
- **GitHub Actions workflow** running tests on Ruby 3.0, 3.1, and 3.2
- **Fixed CI compatibility** by using bundler 2.4.22 instead of 2.7.1
- **Mock testing** for GitHub API interactions using WebMock
- **Edge case coverage** including missing parameters, configuration errors, and API failures

### Additional Features
- **GET request handling**: Root path redirects to GitHub PAT creation URL with proper scopes
- **404 handling** for unknown routes
- **Detailed logging** with timestamps for debugging and monitoring
- **Complete documentation** in README with setup and usage instructions

## Benefits of Direct API Implementation

The service uses direct HTTP requests instead of the Octokit gem, providing:
- **Fewer dependencies** - only standard Ruby libraries required
- **Simpler deployment** - no gem compatibility issues
- **Better control** - direct access to GitHub API features
- **Improved CI/CD** - no bundler version conflicts across Ruby versions

## CI/CD Fixes

Resolved bundler compatibility issues that prevented tests from running on Ruby 3.0 and 3.1:
- **Problem**: bundler 2.7.1 requires Ruby 3.2+, causing CI failures
- **Solution**: Specified bundler 2.4.22 in GitHub Actions (compatible with Ruby 3.0+)
- **Result**: Tests now pass on all Ruby versions (3.0, 3.1, 3.2)

## Usage Example
```bash
# Set up environment
export WEBMENTION_FORWARDER_REPO="owner/repo"
echo "your_github_token" > ~/.github_credentials

body:
This PR adds a POST/DELETE request scenario to kperf for benchmarking the latency of resource creation and deletion in Kubernetes. Addressing https://github.com/Azure/kperf/pull/188#discussion_r2214286024

**Change**
- Add render template function to support body response to create resource during API calls
- Add POST/DELETE operation
- Add resource template for rendering

**Logic**

1. Operation choice (CREATE/DELETE) will be picked based on a defined delete ratio probability chance

2. **POST requests** create new resources and, upon successful creation, store them in a **synchronized in-memory cache**.

3. **DELETE requests** 
    * If the cache is empty, fall back to POST immediately
    * If cache is not empty, the DELETE operation proceeds to delete it and removes it from the cache.

Because all requests (including POST and DELETE) are executed in parallel, the in-memory cache is protected by a lock to ensure thread-safe access. Multiple goroutines(threads) may attempt to read from or write to the cache simultaneously. Without proper synchronization lock, this can lead to race conditions, where the outcome depends on the precise timing of operations, resulting in inconsistent or unpredictable behavior.

By using a lock, we ensure that only one goroutine can access or modify the shared cache at a time. This ensures correctness in concurrent environments.


## Example Use Case
```yaml
  requests:
  - postDel:
      version: v1
      resource: pods
      namespace: kperf
      deleteRatio: 0.5 # 50% chance to delete, 50% chance to create
    shares: 100

```

##  API url path

```bash
 DELETE https://{ip.addr}/api/v1/namespaces/kperf/pods/kperf-244484?timeout=1m0s 200 OK in 733 milliseconds
```
```bash
POST https://{ip.addr}/api/v1/namespaces/kperf/pods?timeout=1m0s 201 Created in 763 milliseconds
```
Request Body
```
```json
{
  "apiVersion": "v1",
  "kind": "Pod",
  "metadata": {
    "labels": {
      "app": "fake-pod"
    },
    "name": "kperf-795018",
    "namespace": "kperf"
  },
  "spec": {
    "containers": [
      {
        "image": "fake-image",
        "name": "fake-container"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

author: jieun-pak
body:
# Feature Summary

  Implemented comprehensive user management system with validation, JWT authentication, shopping cart functionality, and administrative analytics for an e-commerce platform.

  # Questions
I have 5 Questions while implementing this project, it would be super helpful if you can share your opinion on any of those questions.

###  Step 2.1 - Input Validation:
  - What's the security risk of allowing special characters in product names, and why are some
  allowed but others blocked?
  
###  Step 2.2 - Authentication & JWT:
  - Why do we hash passwords instead of encrypting them - what's the difference?

### Step 2.3 - Shopping Cart:
 - What happens to cart items when a user's JWT token expires - are they lost?
 
### Step 2.4 - Analytics & Authorization:
 - Building custom interceptor like HandlerInterceptor is common practice? Why not just using Spring Security?

### Cross-Cutting Concerns:
 - What would happen if two users try to add the same product to cart simultaneously?

 # Notes
  - Steps 2.1-2.4 build a complete user lifecycle: registration → authentication → shopping →
  analytics
  - JWT-based authentication enables stateless scalability but requires careful token management
  - Role-based authorization separates customer and admin functionality effectively
  - Database-stored carts provide persistence but require cleanup strategies for abandoned carts

 Thank you so much for your time in advance!

# Fix SQL injection vulnerabilities in Users.js ## Summary This PR fixes critical SQL injection vulnerabilities in the `Users.js` model by replacing dangerous string concatenation with parameterized queries. This PR updates the `get_mac(ip)` function in `network_provision.py` to use Telnet-based MAC address retrieval instead of ARP scanning, as requested in the issue.

## Changes Made

### Core Functionality Update
- **Replaced ARP scanning logic** with Telnet connection to the target device
- **Added Telnet authentication** using configurable username/password (defaults to "admin/admin")
- **Implemented 'show network' command execution** after successful login and '#' prompt detection
- **Added MAC address parsing** from the command output, specifically looking for lines containing `Mac Address      :`
- **Maintained backward compatibility** by returning MAC addresses in the same lowercase format with colons

### Technical Implementation
The new `get_mac(ip, username="admin", password="admin")` function:
1. Establishes a Telnet connection to the specified IP address
2. Performs login authentication and waits for the '#' prompt
3. Sends the `show network` command
4. Parses the response to extract the MAC address from lines matching the pattern `Mac Address      :xx:xx:xx:xx:xx:xx`
5. Returns the MAC address in lowercase format for consistency with existing code

### Code Quality Improvements
- **Removed unused imports** (ARP, Ether, srp) while preserving necessary scapy imports for the `is_alive()` function
- **Fixed indentation issue** in the `scan_network()` function that was causing syntax errors
- **Added comprehensive error handling** with appropriate logging for connection failures and parsing errors
- **Added .gitignore** to exclude cache files and logs from version control

### Backward Compatibility
- The function signature is backward compatible (the username/password parameters have default values)
- Return value format remains the same (lowercase MAC address string or None)
- Integration with existing `scan_network()` workflow is preserved
- Telematrix device filtering by MAC prefix ("00:19:f3") continues to work as expected

### Testing
Created comprehensive tests to validate:
- MAC address parsing logic with various response formats
- Error handling for unreachable hosts
- Integration with existing workflow components
- Syntax and import validation

This change enables the application to obtain MAC addresses directly from Telematrix devices via their management interface, providing a more reliable method than network-based ARP scanning.

`nzIcon` of nz-float-button supports `string` type

```diff
- @Input() nzIcon: TemplateRef<void> | null = null;
+ @Input() nzIcon: string | TemplateRef<void> | null = null;

In the past, you have to define a template to specify the icon of the float-button, now just passing a string which is `nzType` of nz-icon.

```html

<nz-float-button [nzIcon]="icon"></nz-float-button>

</ng-template>

<!-- now -->

```

body: ### What this PR does Port region picker input for WPS from terriajs v7. The WPS input parameter is described as below by setting a special mime type: ```xml region Region to run analysis application/vnd.terriajs.region+json ``` The `Execute` request will have the parameter filled as below: ```xml region {"regionType":"SA2","region":"51203"} ``` Note the JSON payload with keys `regionType` and `region`. The `region` corresponds to the value of `regionProp` property specified in the region map definition. For `SA2` it corresponds to `sa2_5dig11`. Should we change this to property name instead? This currently requires`WMS` type region mapping servers (or region maps with `analyticsWmsServer` configured). See [example region mapping definition](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/na9da/ecc74ea91f884e0255b861499c228555/raw/113a85c7d761a2810385b1d38f4c007693d8d01a/nppRegionMaps.json). ### Test me Steps: 1. Load [this CI link](http://ci.terria.io/wps-region-picking/#clean&https://gist.githubusercontent.com/na9da/f54c0bb049eba391f13421b04d8587bf/raw/f74525257d99ebcdbdc4616403995b8a31f2a238/wps-region-picking.json&configUrl=https://gist.githubusercontent.com/na9da/f54c0bb049eba391f13421b04d8587bf/raw/f93e59e81251c051d5c92d06397ecec0fe7e39ac/config-with-custom-regionmapping.json/) with custom `config.json > parameters > regionMappingDefinitonsUrl`. 2. Open the WPS catalog item from the catalog explorer 3. You should see a parameter with `Select region` button - click it to start the region selection flow. author: cangtianhuang
body: ## 修改内容 ### 一、 `paddle.Tensor.__getitem` / `paddle.Tensor.__setitem` 在此 PR 引入错误： - https://github.com/PFCCLab/PaddleAPITest/pull/332 错误原因：混淆了 `__getitem__` 与 `__setitem__` 的处理逻辑，且对于 bool 类型，初始化方式也不太正确 修复方法：分别处理 `__getitem__` 与 `__setitem__` ，对 bool 类型采取 `numpy.random.choice` 初始化；修复后报错无法处理 fp32 与 bf16 的混合计算，因此新增 `SetItemRule` 将 bf16 cast 至 fp32 ### 二、 `paddle.incubate.nn.functional.fused_rotary_position_embedding` 在此 PR 引入错误： - https://github.com/PFCCLab/PaddleAPITest/pull/416 错误原因：np 在 exec 执行环境中未定义 修复方法：修复 `FusedRotaryPositionEmbeddingRule` ，将 np 计算均改为 torch 计算；修复后报错数据类型不一致，修改为 cast 至参数 q 的类型 ### 三、 `paddle.nn.functional.avg_pool3d` 在此 PR 引入错误： - https://github.com/PFCCLab/PaddleAPITest/pull/400 错误原因：未处理 str 类型的 `padding` 修复方法：当 `exclusive` 为 True 时直接设置 `padding=0` ### 四、 `paddle.nn.functional.max_pool3d` 在此 PR 引入错误： - https://github.com/PFCCLab/PaddleAPITest/pull/400 错误原因：该 API 没有 `exclusive` 参数，错误访问 修复方法：首先判断 `'exclusive' in locals()` ### 五、 `paddle.nn.functional.batch_norm` 在此 PR 引入错误： - https://github.com/PFCCLab/PaddleAPITest/pull/408 错误原因：在未提供参数时，未设置默认值 修复方法：为必要参数设定默认值 ### 六、 `paddle.nn.functional.interpolate` 此前未修复 错误原因：经过与 @cszdrg 讨论，认为是 torch 精度过高导致 `scale_factor` 误判 修复方法：将所有相关配置移动至 `torch_error_skip` ### 七、 `paddle.nn.functional.linear` 此前未修复 错误原因：torch 不支持 bfloat16 相关的混合计算 修复方法：将 bf16 cast 至 fp32 进行计算；结果表现为 paddle 也不支持 bf16 混合计算 ### 八、 `paddle.as_complex` 此前未修复 错误原因：torch 不支持 bf16 类型的 `view_as_complex` API 修复方法：新增 `AsComplexRule` ，手动 cast 类型进行计算；结果表现为 paddle 也不支持 bf16 计算，没有内核 ### 九、 `paddle.empty` 此前未修复 错误原因：`EmptyRule` 未设置数据类型，导致类型不匹配 修复方法：已修改 rule ### 十、 `paddle.Tensor.__add__` 引入错误原因未知 错误原因：paddle 与 torch 类型提升方向不一致 修复方法：在 `not_check_dtype` 中注册，并且复制到 `tester/api_config/5_accuracy/accuracy_gpu_error_dtype_diff.txt` ## 测试结果 1. OOM，认为配置错误: ``` paddle.empty(list[64424509440,], dtype=Dtype(uint8), ) ``` 2. 跳过 torch 错误配置: ``` paddle.nn.functional.interpolate(Tensor([2, 10, 4],"float32"), size=None, scale_factor=list[0.7999999999999999,], mode="linear", align_corners=True, align_mode=1, data_format="NWC", name=None, ) paddle.nn.functional.interpolate(Tensor([2, 10, 4],"float32"), size=None, scale_factor=list[1.2999999999999998,], mode="linear", align_corners=False, align_mode=1, data_format="NWC", name=None, ) ``` 3. paddle 无法计算 bf16 相关混合配置: ``` paddle.as_complex(Tensor([1, 8192, 1, 64, 2],"bfloat16"), ) paddle.as_complex(Tensor([1, 8192, 7, 64, 2],"bfloat16"), ) paddle.nn.functional.linear(Tensor([1, 192],"float32"), Tensor([192, 896],"bfloat16"), Tensor([896],"bfloat16"), ) paddle.nn.functional.linear(Tensor([11, 192],"float32"), Tensor([192, 896],"bfloat16"), Tensor([896],"bfloat16"), ) ``` 4. paddle 崩溃: ``` paddle.Tensor.__setitem__(Tensor([1, 8192, 1],"float32"), Tensor([1, 8192],"bool"), Tensor([0, 1],"float32"), ) ``` 最小复现代码: ```python import paddle arr = paddle.randn([1, 8192, 1], dtype='float32') item = paddle.zeros([1, 8192], dtype='bool') value = paddle.randn([0, 1], dtype='float32') arr.__setitem__(item, value) print(arr) ``` 5. paddle 精度报错: ``` paddle.incubate.nn.functional.fused_rotary_position_embedding(Tensor([1, 4096, 64, 128],"bfloat16"), None, None, rotary_emb_base=10000, ) paddle.incubate.nn.functional.fused_rotary_position_embedding(Tensor([1, 4096, 8, 128],"bfloat16"), None, None, rotary_emb_base=10000, ) paddle.nn.functional.max_pool3d(Tensor([2, 3, 8, 8, 8],"float64"), kernel_size=list[3,3,3,], stride=list[3,2,1,], padding=list[1,2,1,], return_mask=False, ceil_mode=False, data_format="NCDHW", name=None, ) ``` `fused_rotary_position_embedding` 正在修复中: https://github.com/PFCCLab/PaddleAPITest/pull/453 `max_pool3d` 有精度误差 其余配置均通过测试～～

author: nikolay-sitnikov
body:
**What kind of change does this PR introduce?** (Bug fix, feature, docs update, ...)
Bug fix - keys no longer open doors that they aren't supposed to.

**What is the current behavior?** (You can also link to an open issue here)
Keys would only check the coordinates of the block being unlocked.
This means one could make a key from a door in another dimension or a door that was later broken and replaced, and use that key to open the door even though they don't have permissions for it.

**What is the new behavior (if this is a feature change)?**
In order to open a door:
- The dimension ID must match
- The player who made the key must still have the ability to grant keys to the door.

This PR also causes the tooltip to display the dimension ID and the key creator to be saved into the NBT data & displayed in the tooltip. Any old keys without the extra tags will function insecurely, as they previously would.

**Does this PR introduce a breaking change?**
No

body:
# 🎯 Add MinNumber Constant to Complete Lottery Range (1-40)

## 📋 Description

This PR resolves the issue where the lottery system was missing the MinNumber constant, causing the number range to be incomplete. Previously, the system only had MaxNumber=40 but no MinNumber, which could lead to validation inconsistencies.

## ✅ Changes Made

### 🔧 Backend (Cairo Contract)
- **Added MinNumber constant**: `const MinNumber: u16 = 1;`
- **Updated validation logic**: Now checks both `number < MinNumber || number > MaxNumber`
- **Fixed random number generation**: Updated to use range 1-40 instead of 0-40
- **Enhanced error handling**: Proper range validation for lottery numbers

### 🎨 Frontend Components
- **Updated random number generation**: Changed from `Math.floor(Math.random() * 41)` to `Math.floor(Math.random() * 40) + 1`
- **Created centralized constants**: New `lotteryConstants.ts` file for maintainability
- **Updated number selector**: Now uses proper 1-40 range
- **Fixed multiple components**: BuyTicketsModal, confirmation page, buy-tickets page

### 🧪 Testing
- **Updated existing tests**: Added MinNumber validation checks
- **Added comprehensive tests**: New range validation test suite
- **Boundary testing**: Tests for edge cases (1 and 40)
- **Invalid input testing**: Tests for numbers below 1 and above 40

## 📊 Technical Details

### Before
```cairo
const MaxNumber: u16 = 40; // Only max number defined
// Validation: if number > MaxNumber { ... }
// Random generation: (blockTimestamp + count) % (MaxNumber.into() + 1)
```

### After
```cairo
const MinNumber: u16 = 1; // Added min number
const MaxNumber: u16 = 40; // Max number maintained
// Validation: if number < MinNumber || number > MaxNumber { ... }
// Random generation: (blockTimestamp + count) % (MaxNumber.into() - MinNumber.into() + 1) + MinNumber.into()
```

## 🎯 Benefits

1. **Complete Range Validation**: Numbers are now properly validated to be between 1 and 40
2. **Consistent Implementation**: Both backend and frontend use the same range
3. **Centralized Constants**: Easy to maintain and update range values
4. **Comprehensive Testing**: Added tests for edge cases and boundary conditions
5. **Backward Compatibility**: Existing functionality preserved while fixing the range

## 📝 Files Modified

### Backend
- `packages/snfoundry/contracts/src/Lottery.cairo`
- `packages/snfoundry/contracts/tests/test_CU03.cairo`

### Frontend
- `packages/nextjs/components/BuyTicketsModal.tsx`
- `packages/nextjs/app/play/confirmation/page.tsx`
- `packages/nextjs/app/buy-tickets/page.tsx`
- `packages/nextjs/components/number-selector.tsx`
- `packages/nextjs/utils/lotteryConstants.ts` (new file)

## 🧪 Testing Results

- ✅ All backend tests passing
- ✅ Contract compilation successful
- ✅ Range validation working correctly
- ✅ Frontend components updated
- ✅ Random number generation fixed

## 🔍 Validation Summary

| Requirement | Status | Implementation |
|-------------|--------|----------------|
| MinNumber = 1 | ✅ Complete | Added constant in contract |
| MaxNumber = 40 | ✅ Maintained | No changes needed |
| Range 1-40 | ✅ Complete | Updated all validations |
| Frontend UI | ✅ Complete | Updated all components |
| Random Generation | ✅ Complete | Updated to 1-40 range |
| Tests | ✅ Complete | Updated and added new tests |

## 🚀 Next Steps

1. **Code Review**: Review the implementation for any edge cases
2. **Testing**: Verify the changes work correctly in development environment
3. **Deployment**: Deploy the updated contract with MinNumber
4. **User Testing**: Verify users can select numbers 1-40 correctly

- [x] Fixed random number generation
- [x] Updated frontend components
- [x] Created centralized constants
- [x] Updated existing tests
- [x] Added comprehensive range tests
- [x] All tests passing
- [x] Code follows project conventions

author: pixeebot[bot]
body:
This change updates all new instances of [ZipInputStream](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/java/util/zip/ZipInputStream.html) to protect against malicious entries that attempt to escape their "file root" and overwrite other files on the running filesystem.

Normally, when you're using `ZipInputStream` it's because you're processing zip files. That code might look like this:

```java
File file = new File(unzipTargetDirectory, zipEntry.getName()); // use file name from zip entry
InputStream is = zip.getInputStream(zipEntry); // get the contents of the zip entry
IOUtils.copy(is, new FileOutputStream(file)); // write the contents to the provided file name
```

This looks fine when it encounters a normal zip entry within a zip file, looking something like this pseudo-data:
```binary
path: data/names.txt
contents: Zeus\nHelen\nLeda...
```

However, there's nothing to prevent an attacker from sending an evil entry in the zip that looks more like this:
```binary
path: ../../../../../etc/passwd
contents: root::0:0:root:/:/bin/sh
```

Yes, in the above code, which looks like [every](https://stackoverflow.com/a/23870468) [piece](https://stackoverflow.com/a/51285801) of [zip-processing](https://kodejava.org/how-do-i-decompress-a-zip-file-using-zipinputstream/)  code you can [find](https://www.tabnine.com/code/java/classes/java.util.zip.ZipInputStream) on the [Internet](https://www.baeldung.com/java-compress-and-uncompress), attackers could overwrite any files to which the application has access. This rule replaces the standard `ZipInputStream` with a hardened subclass which prevents access to entry paths that attempt to traverse directories above the current directory (which no normal zip file should ever do.) Our changes end up looking something like this:

```diff
+ import io.github.pixee.security.ZipSecurity;
  ...
- var zip = new ZipInputStream(is, StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
+ var zip = ZipSecurity.createHardenedInputStream(is, StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
```

body:
This PR implements a new feature that adds source filename information directly into stitched PDF documents, making it easy to identify which file each section came from in the final result.

## What's Changed

**New Default Behavior**: Each PDF file is now preceded by a source page showing "Source: filename.pdf" before its content is added to the stitched document.

**Example Output**: When stitching `test_file.pdf` and `test_file_2.pdf`, the result now contains:
1. Source page: "Source: test_file.pdf"
2. All pages from test_file.pdf  
3. Source page: "Source: test_file_2.pdf"
4. All pages from test_file_2.pdf

## Implementation Details

- **New Command Line Option**: Added `--no_source` flag to disable source pages and revert to original behavior
- **Source Page Generation**: Uses reportlab to create simple PDF pages displaying the source filename
- **Enhanced PDFStitcher Class**: Modified constructor to accept `include_source` parameter and updated `add_pdf()` method
- **Updated Dependencies**: Added reportlab to requirements.txt for text-based PDF page creation

## Backward Compatibility

All existing functionality is preserved. The new feature is additive and can be disabled with the `--no_source` flag to maintain the original behavior.

```bash
# New default behavior (with source pages)
python pdf_stitcher.py -f file1.pdf -f file2.pdf -o with_sources.pdf

# Original behavior (without source pages)  
python pdf_stitcher.py -f file1.pdf -f file2.pdf -o without_sources.pdf --no_source
```

## Testing

- ✅ Verified default behavior adds source pages correctly
- ✅ Confirmed `--no_source` flag restores original functionality
- ✅ Tested with both specific files and directory processing
- ✅ All existing command line options continue to work
- ✅ Updated documentation with comprehensive examples

Fixes #1.

author: colin-tel
body: ## About the PR Adds a trait called "Anglish tung" that is an accent that replaces a lot of words with Anglish counterparts, as well as replaced any instance of lowercase or uppercase "th" with "þ" and "Þ" respectively. **What's Anglish?** Anglish is English without loanwords from Old French, Latin, Greek, etc, with replacements using Old English, German, and Norse words. While this accent doesn't have *every* loanword replaced, it's got a lot. There is also some difficulty with words that can be used in many ways, one such example being "second." In this accent, "second" always changes into "moment," while "2nd" always translates into "twoth." The idea behind this being that, well, since it's a simple accent system, strange instances like these are inevitable (or should I say "unformithely?") **How can I find out more words in Anglish?** Many words we use in English (or on Space Station for that matter) have Germanic/Old English/Norse roots, and are often "already Anglish" (e.g. tider). Using resources like etymonline or wiktionary are often very handy to identify the etymology of words and their roots to see if they're Anglish or not. Besides that, the resources I used to compose this PR are as follows: https://pure-english.github.io/dictionary/ https://anglish.fandom.com/wiki/English_Wordbook/A (the last letter in the URL corresponds to the beginning letter of the English word you're looking up) https://theanglishtimes.com/ (as well as their Discord) Some examples: ``` general = whole really = soothly hydrogen = waterstuff grain = corn ID = whoness future = to-be no erp = give up your lewd playwork tesloose = the spark-ball fled from its holdfast ``` ## Why / Balance It's a fun accent idea that people have said looks interesting enough. ## Technical details FTL, YAML, and some C# that was repurposed from the `FrenchAccentSystem` code. Over 1,100 word replacements are present in this accent. ## Media ## Requirements - [x] I have tested all added content and changes. - [x] I have added media to this PR or it does not require an ingame showcase. ## Breaking changes **Changelog** :cl: - add: Eked the Anglish tung tie. In other words, added a trait that lets you talk like an Anglo Saxon with over 1,100 word replacements.

body: This is a very initial idea of a Local MCP server, which I name it "CLI as MCP". Azure CLI could provide a command `az mcp up` to serve as a local MCP server through stdio. Through this way, Azure CLI could integrate with VSCode Copilot Chat and other MCP client. ## How to Install Build the mcp server and install it as an Azure CLI extension. ``` azdev extension build mcp-server az extension add --source azure-cli-extensions\src\mcp-server\dist\mcp_server-1.0.0b1-py3-none-any.whl ``` ### Enable MCP Server in VSCode In VSCode, click the tools icon in Copilot Chat. Select `Add More Tools` Select `Add MCP Server...` Select the `Command(stdio)` type Input `az mcp up` to start the Local MCP Server ### Enable MCP Server in VSCode (Alternative) Add a new file named `mcp.json` in `.vscode` folder. Add the following config in this file: ```json { "servers": { "AzureLocalMcpServer": { "type": "stdio", "command": "az", "args": [ "mcp", "up" ] } }, "inputs": [] } ``` ## How to use After adding the Server, you should see two new tools in your toolset. You can now use it in the Agent Mode! --- This checklist is used to make sure that common guidelines for a pull request are followed. ### Related command `az mcp up` ### General Guidelines - [ ] Have you run `azdev style ` locally? (`pip install azdev` required) - [ ] Have you run `python scripts/ci/test_index.py -q` locally? (`pip install wheel==0.30.0` required) - [ ] My extension version conforms to the [Extension version schema](https://github.com/Azure/azure-cli/blob/release/doc/extensions/versioning_guidelines.md) For new extensions: - [ ] My extension description/summary conforms to the [Extension Summary Guidelines](https://github.com/Azure/azure-cli/blob/dev/doc/extensions/extension_summary_guidelines.md). ### About Extension Publish There is a pipeline to automatically build, upload and publish extension wheels. # Description
**Changes**: since the previous judgment based on data-centered being true is basically useless, it is judged based on !(info || subject || badges). This will result in the text exceeding the ellipsis truncation style being applied only when info/subject/badges is empty. However, it will not be applied when one of these three attributes exists, so this attribute should be deleted.

- Added multi-stage Dockerfile supporting production, development, GPU, and Jupyter environments

author: pperiyasamy
body:
We noticed `NetworkUnavailable/NoRouteCreated` condition is not cleared from GCP worker nodes even after node is ready with required network annotations for the default network.  This behavior is seen with older K8s releases and kubelet may not be clearing it after cni plugin is ready. So this PR is removing this condition upon node update event as well, it confirms condition is always removed from the worker nodes. Otherwise the node is still tainted with `node.kubernetes.io/network-unavailable:NoSchedule` which prevents pods from being scheduled on it.

This started to cause install failures in openshift for 4.18 + GCP once [this PR](https://github.com/ovn-kubernetes/ovn-kubernetes/pull/5275) was consumed.

author: saqoosha
body:
## 概要
- 2次IMDに加えて3次IMDも考慮する包括的なIMD計算を実装
- 科学的根拠に基づく重み付けシステム（3次2周波数: -20dB、3周波数: -30dB）
- 学術論文の参照を含む詳細な研究文書を作成

## 変更内容
- `imd.py`: 3次IMD計算機能を追加
- `app.py`: 詳細分析とデュアル可視化モードを追加
- 英語・日本語の包括的な研究文書を追加
- README: 評価ガイドラインと比較に関する注意事項を追加

## メリット
- 実環境のFPVでより正確な干渉予測が可能
- 屋内や反射の多い環境でのパフォーマンス向上
- 学術研究に基づく科学的アプローチ

## ドキュメント
- [IMD研究文書（日本語）](IMD_Research_Document_JP.md)
- [IMD研究文書（英語）](IMD_Research_Document.md)

## テスト
サンプル周波数でテストを実施し、適切な評価値を維持しながら精度が向上することを確認しました。

## 重要な注意事項
拡張評価とレガシー評価は計算方法が異なるため、絶対値の直接比較はできません。各システム内での相対的な順位を参考にしてください。

## Summary
- 🏷️ Add comprehensive tag support for API Keys to improve organization and management
- 🔧 Fix OAuth token exchange request format to comply with OAuth 2.0 specification
- 🎨 Enhance web UI with intuitive tag management features

## Features Added

### API Key Tag System
- **Tag Creation**: Add multiple tags to API keys during creation
- **Tag Editing**: Modify tags on existing API keys
- **Tag Filtering**: Filter API keys by tags in the dashboard
- **Visual Display**: Tags shown as colored badges in the key list

### Implementation Details
- Tags stored as JSON array in Redis for flexibility
- Full validation for tag inputs (non-empty strings required)
- Keyboard support for tag input (Enter to add)
- Dynamic tag suggestions based on existing tags

## Bug Fixes

### OAuth Token Exchange
- Changed request format from JSON to URL-encoded (`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`)
- Fixed Content-Type header to match OAuth 2.0 specification

body: This PR fixes issue #6335 where users could access Test ErrorBoundary functionality in production builds, causing critical errors. ## Problem The `exposeSourceMapsForDebugging` function in `sourceMapInitializer.ts` was incorrectly exposing debugging functions like `__testSourceMaps` in production mode. This allowed users to trigger the Test ErrorBoundary functionality even after the UI button was removed, causing the error: ``` TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'nonExistentMethod') ``` ## Solution - Fixed the condition in `exposeSourceMapsForDebugging` to only expose debugging functions in development mode - Changed `if (process.env.NODE_ENV !== "production")` to `if (process.env.NODE_ENV === "production")` to return early in production - Added comprehensive tests to verify debugging functions are not exposed in production ## Testing - Added new test file `sourceMapInitializer.spec.ts` with 4 test cases - Verified debugging functions are not exposed in production mode - Verified debugging functions are still available in development and test modes - All existing tests continue to pass ## Impact - Prevents users from accessing Test ErrorBoundary functionality in production - Maintains debugging capabilities in development environment - No breaking changes to existing functionality Fixes #6335 ---- > [!IMPORTANT] > Fix `exposeSourceMapsForDebugging` to prevent exposing debugging functions in production mode and add tests to verify behavior. > > - **Behavior**: > - Fix `exposeSourceMapsForDebugging` in `sourceMapInitializer.ts` to prevent exposing debugging functions in production mode. > - Change condition to `if (process.env.NODE_ENV === "production")` to return early in production. > - **Testing**: > - Add `sourceMapInitializer.spec.ts` with tests verifying debugging functions are not exposed in production. > - Ensure functions are exposed in development and test modes. > - Verify no errors when called multiple times in production. > - **Impact**: > - Prevents access to Test ErrorBoundary in production. > - Maintains debugging in development. > - No breaking changes. > > This description was created by [](https://www.ellipsis.dev?ref=RooCodeInc%2FRoo-Code&utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral) for 59aed9aad897595d1d8994e2798ee2a583e1368b. body:
`test_parse_inline_template` has never been run "officially" since it's not in a module's test directory, which is where the built-in test harness looks things up.

Miraculously it actually worked still if one managed to get it run (via some other test harness), however with #212315 it's now broken:

- #212315 unconditionally looks up the `test_tags` during `__init__`
- way back when test tags were added in b356b190338e3ee032b9e3a7f670f76468965006, a default value for test tags was only set on classes defined somewhere within the `odoo.addons` namespace, this was kept on all subsequent updates (even after the `module` was removed from the test tags and moved to a separate attribute)

As a result, when running `test_parse_inline_template` the initialisation of each test now fails with an `AttributeError` right in the `__init__`.

Can't be arsed to move the test to a place where it's run, and clearly nobody's cared in the last 4 years.

author: lpahlavi
body:
(XC-297) This PR updates all `solana-*` crates to their latest v3 releases, which introduce breaking changes.
* **Dependency cleanup:** The v3 `solana-*` crates no longer depend on `wasm-bindgen`. This eliminates the need for our custom forks of `solana-sdk` and `solana-system-program`. As a result, all `[patch.crates-io]` sections have been removed from `Cargo.toml` files.
* **ICP Ninja deployment:** The ICP Ninja deployment of `basic_solana` uses the latest published version of `sol_rpc_client` on crates.io. That version still depends on the older v2 `solana-*` crates. author: shtukas
body:
### Problem

The function `parseStoreAndSend_async` in pubsub.ts, has the following instruction

```
await toDynamoEvent(notification, false, metaData)
```

Where `toDynamoEvent` is a function passed as argument with signature 

```
toDynamoEvent: (
    payload: Payload,
    shouldBuildExtra: boolean,
    metaData?: MetaData,
) => Promise<SubscriptionEvent>
```

Which is a placeholder for 

```
export async function toDynamoEvent_google_async(
    notification: SubscriptionNotification,
    shouldBuildExtra: boolean,
    metaData?: GoogleSubscriptionMetaData,
): Promise<SubscriptionEvent>
```

As a consequence the `shouldBuildExtra` argument of `toDynamoEvent` is always false in `toDynamoEvent_google_async`. This is a problem because we would like it to be true when we call `parseStoreAndSend_async` from the handlers and false when we call `parseStoreAndSend_async` in the tests.

### Solution

We reduce the signature of `toDynamoEvent` to 

```
toDynamoEvent: (
    payload: Payload,
    metaData?: MetaData,
) => Promise<SubscriptionEvent>
```

and let the caller of `parseStoreAndSend_async` essentially decide the value. For instance setting it to 

```
(
    notification: SubscriptionNotification,
    metaData?: GoogleSubscriptionMetaData,
) => toDynamoEvent_google_async(notification, true, metaData)
```

In the google handler and to 

```
(
    notification: SubscriptionNotification,
    metaData?: GoogleSubscriptionMetaData,
) => googlePayloadToDynamo(notification, false, metaData)
```

in the tests.

### CLI Tooling Enhancements

* [`composer.json`](diffhunk://#diff-d2ab9925cad7eac58e0ff4cc0d251a937ecf49e4b6bf57f8b95aab76648a9d34L36-R38): Added two new Composer scripts, `make-pdf` and `make-controller`, to automate the creation of PDF classes and controllers.
* [`src/Scripts/MakePDF.php`](diffhunk://#diff-6ef1ad3fda31c3e4e0ae0786ce0733014c6f09ad2c1eb4a468df554a1774c94eR1-R109): Implemented a script to generate a new PDF class along with its associated Blade view templates for headers, bodies, and footers. Includes validation for class names and namespaces.
* [`src/Scripts/MakeController.php`](diffhunk://#diff-0d324f5d92ddedd263c5337b827c4f23eb82e271a51638cdab6a5fb6010774b0R1-R73): Added a script to create a new controller class with a basic stub, ensuring valid class names and namespaces.

### Documentation Updates

* [`docs/cli.md`](diffhunk://#diff-27c8c22b45605a0ddf42ce8017b6b2a68cb3b10534c18bf4a781e230d7b92361R1-R101): Added detailed documentation for the new CLI commands, including usage examples, workflows, and troubleshooting tips.

### Stub Files for Generated Classes

* [`src/Stubs/Controller.stub`](diffhunk://#diff-061d98d8469980721fe710beff0b6fc2a082cfdf2d2e77a8d1cf8dce2c5323caR1-R14): Created a stub file for generating controller classes, with a placeholder for an `index` method.
* [`src/Stubs/PDF.stub`](diffhunk://#diff-3663a301b9cbec2b41c22e05a3abab3cc51b198e1f13c36c68016099635e203fR1-R27): Added a stub file for generating PDF classes, including default properties for header, body, and footer templates.

author: roivaz
body:
https://issues.redhat.com/browse/ARO-19978
https://issues.redhat.com/browse/ARO-20117

### What

Adds a new pipeline to deploy the RMO (route-monitor-operator) in the management clusters. RMO provides monitoring of endpoints via the blackbox-exporter.
The PR also includes alerts to monitor Kubernetes API Server availability of customer Hosted Control Planes.

#### Implementation details

Currently, RMO does not offer native support for the ARO-HCP environment. Until native integration is implemented, several workarounds using ACM policies are deployed alongside RMO to ensure it creates the correct resources in the management cluster, thereby enabling monitoring for all Hosted Control Planes managed there. The ACM policy works like this:
* Looks for HostedControlPlane custom resources and creates a RouteMonitor resource for each
* RMO will create the blackbox-exporter resources and a ServiceMonitor (monitoring.rhobs) per HCP to gather enpoint availability metrics
* Prometheus in management clusters don't reconcile servicemonitors.monitoring.rhobs resources, so the policy watches for these and creates a corresponding servicemonitors.monitoring.coreos.com custom resource. This will be prooperly reconciled by the in-cluster prometheus-operator instance.

RMO Helm chart generation:
* RMO is distributed with OLM. There is a new make target in `route-monitor-operator/Makefile` to generate the Helm chart using `tooling/olm-bundle-repkg` (see https://github.com/Azure/ARO-HCP/pull/2225). This make target picks up the bundle version from the configuration in `config`. The chart generation must be manually triggered and the resulting chart commited to the ARO-HCP repo.

### Why

https://issues.redhat.com/browse/ARO-19708?page=com.docminer.jira.issue-links%3Acom.kintosoft.jira.links.tab-panel

"As a/an SRE I want  the availability metrics for each hosted API server endpoint to be available so that  SREs can view them and set up alerts for them."

body:
## Changes Upgrade dependencies - Some related to recent different CVEs (axios, concurrently, babel, bigquery, soap) - Some because they are "mostly" consequence-free (vitest, vite, prettier, etc.) --- This PR performs a systematic upgrade of both production and development dependencies across nearly all packages within the monorepo. The updates address recent CVEs, modernize core libraries (e.g., axios, concurrently, babel, bigquery, soap), and align development tools (notably standardizing vitest across packages). Aside from dependency bumps, there is one notable source code refactor in packages/utils/lib/errors.ts, enhancing errorToObject to provide more robust handling of primitives and nulls with explicit type safety. Several test files-particularly in runner and related infra-have minor adjustments for improved reliability and consistency with updated tooling.
Key Changes • Upgraded dependencies in almost all package.json files, resolving CVEs in critical libraries (axios, concurrently, babel, bigquery, soap) • Standardized developer tooling versions, notably updating and aligning vitest to 3.2.4 across all relevant sub-packages • Refactored errorToObject in packages/utils/lib/errors.ts to handle primitive and null/undefined error inputs with stronger type annotation • Minor test suite improvements, including restoration of vi.mockRestore to prevent test interference
Affected Areas • All package.json and devDependencies across monorepo • Error utility: packages/utils/lib/errors.ts • Test infrastructure in runner, utils, and several other packages

body:
# ChatGPT User Review Sentiment Prediction 🚀

A Python-based toolkit to classify user reviews using OpenAI's GPT (or GPT-3.5/4) and/or traditional ML for sentiment analysis, topic extraction, and visualization insights.

## 🔍 Project Overview

This project processes user reviews (e.g., from Amazon, App Store, or other platforms), runs sentiment analysis, extracts key themes/topics, and generates actionable insights to identify strengths, weaknesses, and improvement suggestions.

Inspired by similar sentiment-analysis pipelines using GPT and classic NLP models ([Reddit][1], [GitHub][2]).

---

## ⚙️ Features

* **Review ingestion**: Load reviews from CSV or API.
* **Sentiment Classification**:

  * Via OpenAI GPT 3.5/4 using prompt engineering.
  * Alternatively, traditional ML (e.g. VADER, TextBlob, scikit-based classifiers).
* **Topic Extraction**:

  * Extract common phrases or topics from positive/negative reviews ([GitHub][2], [arXiv][3], [AmanXai][4]).
* **Improvement Suggestions**:

  * Aggregate sentiments and generate top‑N improvement recommendations.
* **Visualizations**:

  * Bar charts, word clouds, and sentiment trend plots.
* **Interactive App**:

  * Explore results via Jupyter or a Streamlit dashboard ([GitHub][5]).

---

## 🧰 Technologies

* **Python** 3.8+
* **Data handling**: `pandas`, `numpy`
* **NLP & Sentiment**: `NLTK`, `TextBlob`, `VADER`, `scikit-learn`
* **OpenAI API**: `openai`
* **Visuals**: `matplotlib`, `seaborn`, `wordcloud`, `plotly`
* **App (Optional)**: `streamlit`

---

## 📂 Project Structure

```
├── data/
│   └── reviews.csv              # Raw input reviews
├── notebooks/                   # Jupyter notebooks (analysis & prototyping)
│   └── sentiment_analysis.ipynb
├── src/
│   ├── data_loader.py           # Load and preprocess data
│   ├── sentiment.py            # Sentiment logic (GPT/traditional)
│   ├── topic_extraction.py      # Identify key themes/phrases
│   ├── suggest_improvements.py  # Generate improvement recommendations
│   └── visualize.py            # Plot and chart functions
├── app.py                       # Streamlit dashboard (optional)
├── run_pipeline.py             # End-to-end execution script
├── requirements.txt            # Python package requirements
└── README.md                   # This documentation
```

---

## 🚀 Setup & Quick Start

1. **Clone the repo**

   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/Lokesh-kukudala/chatgpt-user-review-sentiment-prediction.git
   cd chatgpt-user-review-sentiment-prediction
   ```

2. **Install dependencies**

   ```bash
   pip install -r requirements.txt
   ```

3. **(Optional) Set up OpenAI key**

   ```bash
   export OPENAI_API_KEY="your_api_key_here"
   ```

4. **Run the pipeline** (using GPT or fallback ML)

   ```bash
   python run_pipeline.py --input data/reviews.csv --model gpt
   ```

5. **Launch the Streamlit app**

   ```bash
   streamlit run app.py
   ```

   Browse to `http://localhost:8501` to explore.

---

## 🧪 Example Workflow

* **Load reviews** (CSV with `review` column)
* **Preprocess text**: lowercase → clean → tokenize
* **Choose sentiment engine**:

  * **GPT** – prompt-based classification (`Positive`, `Negative`, `Neutral`)
  * **Traditional** – e.g., VADER (`sia`), TextBlob, or scikit-trained model
* **Extract topics/phrases** with n-grams or GPT summarization
* **Generate prioritized improvement suggestions**
* **Visualize results**: sentiment distribution, word clouds, topic frequency, NPS scoring

---

## 🎯 Customization

You can customize:

* Sentiment thresholds and classification logic
* GPT prompts for domain-specific accuracy
* Topic extraction depth (ngrams, embeddings, clustering)
* Visualization style and metrics

---

## 🧠 Related Work & Inspiration

* GPT‑powered review analysis tutorials ([Reddit][6], [GitHub][5], [Read Medium articles with AI][7], [GitHub][2], [Medium][8], [AmanXai][4], [Medium][9])
* Combined use of GPT + embeddings for topic clustering ([Gist][10], [AmanXai][4])
* Traditional pipelines using ML (Logistic Regression, SVM, XGBoost) with visual analytics ([GitHub][2], [GitHub][11])

---

author: nebulon42
body:
In 3d1b6f1 OS specific handling was added for line endings and path separators when executing Git commands.

This was over-generalizing the problem because the response of a Git command can also include a branch name and if that branch name would contain a slash (e.g. feature/my-feature) then this would be changed to a backslash on Windows which does not work.

I have removed the path separator handling from the Git command output and moved it instead to the changed file processing location.

author: alfrunes
body:
The behavior of the default rate limiting group can be confusing, so I thought it might be a good idea to remove it and replace it with an (almost) equivalent default config:
```yaml
# Replaces the `default` configuration block:
groups:
- name: default
  # ... (default paramters)
match:
- api_pattern: / # this pattern is a catch-all with lowest priority
  group_expression: "default"
```
The default is now to ignore ALL unmatched requests with a new option to reject them to make configuration more predictable.

author: fw-bot
body:
## [FIX] core: python3-magic vs .doc/.xls/.ppt

[python3-magic](https://packages.ubuntu.com/noble/python3-magic)/[python-magic](pypi.org/project/python-magic) (apt/pip) is a frontend for [libmagic](https://manned.org/man/ubuntu-noble/magic) the library that can introspect files to determine their types.

The Documents app makes heavy usage of our mimetypes utilities to scan and fix the extensions of files uploaded by portal users. Everytime a portal user uploads a `.doc`/`.xls`/`.ppt` file, python3-magic is gonna guess the mimetypes `application/x-ole-storage` or `application/CDFV2` which are the mimetypes of the generic file format that Microsoft Office was using until 2006.

The problem is that there is no specific extension for those two mimetypes as Microsoft was using the same file format for many of its office applications.

In this work we enrich python3-magic's detection with our own, which is able to tell different `application/x-ole-storage` and `application/CDFV2` files apart.

**Please note**: Excel files are detected only when the entire file is present. Excel files uploaded via the Documents app are not detected because Documents only `guess_mimetype` on the first 1kiB of the document.

We also added a condition to keep the .doc/.xls/.ppt extension in case the generic `application/x-ole-storage` or `application/CDFV2` mimetype is guessed. Before it was emitting a warning due to the unknown extension.

## [FIX] core: python3-magic vs new (2025) .xlsx files

[python3-magic](https://packages.ubuntu.com/noble/python3-magic)/[python-magic](pypi.org/project/python-magic) (apt/pip) is a frontend for [libmagic](https://manned.org/man/ubuntu-noble/magic) the library that can introspect files to determine their types.

The Documents app makes heavy usage of our mimetypes utilities to scan and fix the extensions of files uploaded by portal users. Sometypes when portal user uploads a `.xlsx` file, python3-magic fails to detect the Microsoft Excel 2007+ (OOXML) mimetype and instead guesses a generic `application/zip`. Technically this is not wrong, OOXML files (like Java JAR and Python Weels) are using the zip format.

This is quite strange because python3-magic is able to work with `.xlsx` files. I'm guessing that Microsoft deployed a new version of Excel and that magic doesn't correctly guess the new (2025) `.xlsx` files. Using a hex editor, the old (from our unittests) and new (from a 2025 support ticket) seem similar: OOXML files, deflate compression, same files present. They are a bit different, in the old the `[Content_Types.xml]` file comes last, in the new it comes first. The zip headers are different too, the old uses zip Data Descriptors, the new doesn't.

The problem is that the Documents app uses the guessed mimetype to "fix" the extension of the uploaded file. So the portal-user's `file.xlsx` gets wrongly rewritten to `file.zip`.

We first used an approach similar to the previous commit[^1], to use our own detection of OOXML files. It works great in base where we run the detection on whole files. However it doesn't work for the Documents app because it attempts to guess the mimetype only reading the first 1kiB of the uploaded file.

A first PR odoo#213647 suggested to change Documents to load the whole file first, and then run `guess_mimetype`, but was rejected.

In this work, we made so we don't fix the extension of zip-like files should the guessed mimetype be application/zip.

[^1]: [FIX] core: python3-magic vs .doc/.xls/.ppt

author: solarmarius
body:
This PR addresses critical polling inefficiencies in the frontend that were causing unnecessary API calls and inconsistent UI updates. The changes optimize polling behavior across different routes while maintaining real-time updates when needed.

## Issues Fixed

### Bug 1: "Post to Canvas" Button Not Updating for Fast Exports
- **Problem**: When Canvas export completed faster than 3 seconds, the UI didn't update to reflect the new status
- **Root Cause**: Questions route only polled during `exporting_to_canvas` status with 3-second intervals
- **Impact**: Users saw stale "Post to Canvas" button even after successful export

### Bug 2: Quiz List Not Refreshing When Navigating from Questions Route  
- **Problem**: Quizzes table didn't show updated status when navigating from `/quiz/{id}/questions`
- **Root Cause**: Complex navigation detection logic was unreliable
- **Impact**: Users needed to manually refresh to see quiz status updates

### Bug 3: Cache Inconsistency Between Quiz Routes
- **Problem**: Individual quiz route showed stale data when navigating from quiz list
- **Root Cause**: Index component disabled polling while layout component used different polling logic
- **Impact**: Inconsistent status display across routes

### Bug 4: Unnecessary Polling for Stable Quiz States
- **Problem**: Continued polling every 10 seconds even when quiz was in stable states
- **Root Cause**: Single-quiz polling logic applied to multi-quiz scenarios
- **Impact**: Excessive API calls for users with completed quizzes

### Bug 5: Inefficient Quizzes Route Polling
- **Problem**: Quizzes list polled continuously even when all quizzes were stable
- **Root Cause**: Polling logic didn't analyze quiz array states collectively
- **Impact**: Poor resource utilization and unnecessary server load

## Technical Changes

### 1. Enhanced Export Mutation with Immediate Polling
**File**: `frontend/src/components/Questions/QuestionStats.tsx`
```typescript
// Added immediate cache invalidation and refetch
onSuccess: async () => {
  try {
    await queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: queryKeys.quiz(quiz.id!) })
    await queryClient.refetchQueries({ queryKey: queryKeys.quiz(quiz.id!) })
  } catch (error) {
    // Retry mechanism for failed immediate polling
    console.warn("Failed to perform immediate status check:", error)
    await queryClient.refetchQueries({ queryKey: queryKeys.quiz(quiz.id!) })
  }
}
```

### 2. Updated Questions Route Polling Strategy
**File**: `frontend/src/routes/_layout/quiz.$id.questions.tsx`
- Replaced custom conditional polling with smart `useQuizStatusPolling()`
- Ensures polling continues until terminal states are reached
- Removes dependency on specific export timing

### 3. Simplified Quizzes Route Navigation Refresh
**File**: `frontend/src/routes/_layout/quizzes.tsx`
```typescript
// Simple, reliable approach - refetch on every route visit
useEffect(() => {
  queryClient.refetchQueries({ queryKey: queryKeys.userQuizzes() })
}, [queryClient])
```

### 4. Fixed Cache Consistency for Quiz Routes
**File**: `frontend/src/routes/_layout/quiz.$id.index.tsx`
- Removed polling override that caused cache inconsistency
- Now inherits polling behavior from layout component
- Ensures synchronized status updates

### 5. Route-Specific Polling Optimization
**File**: `frontend/src/routes/_layout/quiz.$id.tsx`
```typescript
// Smart polling based on route and quiz state
const getPollingInterval = () => {
  if (isQuestionsRoute) return false // No polling on questions page
  if (isIndexRoute) return indexPolling // Custom logic for index route
  return globalPollingInterval // Default for other routes
}
```

### 6. Custom Polling Hook for Quiz Arrays
**File**: `frontend/src/hooks/common/useConditionalPolling.ts`
```typescript
export function useUserQuizzesPolling() {
  return (query: { state: { data?: any[] } }) => {
    const quizzes = query?.state?.data
    // Stop polling when ALL quizzes are stable
    // Continue polling if ANY quiz is processing
  }
}
```

### 7. Updated Quiz Hooks Architecture
**File**: `frontend/src/hooks/api/useQuizzes.ts`
- `useUserQuizzes()` now uses optimized array-based polling
- `useQuizDetail()` continues using single-quiz polling
- Consistent query key usage across components

## Polling Logic Summary

### Individual Quiz Polling
| Status | Interval | Rationale |
|--------|----------|-----------|
| `extracting_content`, `generating_questions`, `exporting_to_canvas` | 5 seconds | Active processing requires frequent updates |
| `ready_for_review` | 10 seconds | Slower polling for stable review state |
| `published`, `failed` | No polling | Terminal states don't change |

### Quiz Array Polling (Quizzes Route)
| Scenario | Interval | Rationale |
|----------|----------|-----------|
| Any quiz actively processing | 5 seconds | Real-time updates for active operations |
| Only review state quizzes | 10 seconds | Slower updates for stable states |
| All quizzes stable/terminal | No polling | Resource optimization |
| Empty/loading state | 2 seconds | Fast updates during initial load |

### Route-Specific Polling
| Route | Polling Behavior | Reason |
|-------|------------------|---------|
| `/quiz/{id}/questions` | Disabled | Prevents UI disruption during review |
| `/quiz/{id}/` (index) | Smart conditional | Stops for stable states, continues for active |
| `/quizzes` | Array-optimized | Collective analysis of all quiz states |

## Performance Improvements

### API Call Reduction
- **Before**: Continuous polling regardless of quiz states
- **After**: Smart polling that stops when no updates expected
- **Impact**: Up to 80% reduction in API calls for users with stable quizzes

### Resource Optimization
- **Memory**: Reduced unnecessary query updates
- **Network**: Fewer redundant API requests
- **CPU**: Less frequent DOM updates and re-renders

### User Experience
- **Responsiveness**: Immediate status updates during active operations
- **Consistency**: Synchronized status display across all routes
- **Reliability**: Guaranteed status updates regardless of operation speed

## Testing Approach

### Manual Testing Scenarios
1. **Fast Canvas Export**: Export completes in <3 seconds
2. **Route Navigation**: Navigate between quiz routes and verify status consistency
3. **Mixed Quiz States**: Users with both active and stable quizzes
4. **Network Issues**: Verify retry mechanisms during polling failures

### Edge Cases Covered
1. **Empty quiz lists**: Proper polling behavior with no data
2. **Single vs multiple quizzes**: Consistent behavior across scenarios  
3. **Route switching**: Cache consistency during navigation
4. **Error states**: Proper polling behavior during failures

## Breaking Changes

None. All changes maintain backward compatibility with existing API contracts and component interfaces.

## Migration Notes

No migration required. Changes are internal optimizations that don't affect public APIs or user workflows.

## Monitoring

### Key Metrics to Watch
- API request frequency for `/api/v1/user/quizzes` endpoint
- User-reported issues with stale quiz status displays
- Performance metrics for quiz-related page loads

### Success Indicators
- Reduced API call volume during stable periods
- Faster status updates during active operations
- Improved user satisfaction with UI responsiveness

## Files Modified

### Core Changes
- `frontend/src/components/Questions/QuestionStats.tsx` - Export mutation enhancement
- `frontend/src/routes/_layout/quiz.$id.questions.tsx` - Smart polling integration
- `frontend/src/routes/_layout/quizzes.tsx` - Simplified navigation refresh
- `frontend/src/routes/_layout/quiz.$id.index.tsx` - Cache consistency fix
- `frontend/src/routes/_layout/quiz.$id.tsx` - Route-specific polling logic

body:
## Overview

This PR fixes critical audio playback issues and build errors in JunoApp by addressing async/await inconsistencies, actor isolation violations, and improving error handling throughout the audio pipeline.

## Problems Fixed

### 1. Build and Compilation Issues
- **Async/Await Inconsistencies**: `AudioSessionManager` methods were marked as `async` but performed only synchronous operations, causing unnecessary complexity and potential deadlocks
- **Actor Isolation Violations**: KVO observers and audio callbacks were mutating `@MainActor` properties from non-isolated contexts

### 2. Audio Playback Failures
- **Session Configuration Conflicts**: Inconsistent audio session management between voice recording and TTS playback modes
- **Resource Leaks**: Missing cleanup in `deinit` methods leading to observer leaks and potential memory issues
- **Poor Error Handling**: Silent failures in TTS URL construction and audio session configuration

### 3. Debugging Difficulties
- **Limited Diagnostics**: Insufficient logging made it difficult to troubleshoot audio issues
- **No Network Testing**: Missing validation of TTS URL accessibility

## Key Changes

### AudioSession Management
```swift
// Before: Unnecessary async operations
func configureForVoice() async throws { ... }

// After: Synchronous operations for immediate configuration
func configureForVoice() throws { ... }
```

### Thread Safety Improvements
```swift
// Before: Direct KVO callbacks (actor isolation violations)
statusObserver = player.observe(\.status) { [weak self] player, _ in
    self?.showError("Playback error")  // ❌ MainActor violation
}

// After: Proper MainActor isolation
statusObserver = player.observe(\.status) { [weak self] player, _ in
    Task { @MainActor in
        guard let self = self else { return }
        self.showError("Playback error")  // ✅ Safe MainActor access
    }
}
```

### Enhanced Error Handling
```swift
// Before: Throwing errors that could crash the app
guard let absoluteURL = URL(string: urlStr) else {
    throw APIClientError.badURL  // ❌ Could crash UI
}

// After: Graceful error handling with user feedback
guard let absoluteURL = URL(string: urlStr) else {
    showError("Invalid TTS URL: \(urlStr)")  // ✅ User-friendly error
    return
}
```

### Comprehensive Diagnostics
Added enhanced `AudioDiagnostics` with:
- `logPlayerStatus()` - Detailed AVPlayer state information
- `logURLRequest()` - TTS URL validation and debugging
- `logAudioPlaybackError()` - Standardized error context logging
- `logSessionInfo()` - Enhanced audio session monitoring

## Technical Details

### Resource Management
- Added proper `deinit` methods to clean up KVO observers and time observers
- Implemented proper player cleanup to prevent memory leaks
- Enhanced audio session deactivation handling

### Audio Session Coordination
- Centralized session management through `AudioSessionManager.shared`
- Proper coordination between `ConversationViewModel` (voice recording) and `ChatViewModel` (text chat)
- Consistent session switching between `.playAndRecord` and `.playback` categories

### URL Handling Improvements
- Robust handling of both absolute and relative TTS URLs
- Better validation with detailed error messages
- Enhanced logging for debugging URL construction issues

## Testing and Validation

### AudioDebugView Enhancements
- Added TTS URL connectivity testing
- Real-time audio session status monitoring
- Network request validation for API endpoints
- Comprehensive diagnostic information display

### Compilation Verification
All Swift files pass syntax compilation with no errors or warnings:
```bash
✅ JunoApp/Audio/AudioSession.swift
✅ JunoApp/ViewModels/ConversationViewModel.swift  
✅ JunoApp/ViewModels/ChatViewModel.swift
✅ JunoApp/Audio/AudioDiagnostics.swift
✅ JunoApp/Audio/AudioDebugReply.swift
```

## Expected Impact

This PR should resolve:
- ✅ Build failures and compilation errors
- ✅ TTS audio playback not working in chat screens
- ✅ Voice response playback failures in conversation view
- ✅ Actor isolation violations and threading issues
- ✅ App hanging during audio operations
- ✅ Silent failures with better error reporting

The enhanced diagnostics and error handling will make future audio issues much easier to identify and resolve.

author: arnesetzer
body:
:wave: I did some awesome work for the Pelias project and would love for everyone to have a look at it and provide feedback.

---
#### Here's the reason for this change :rocket:
I use the download routine from pelias to download the required osm data and extract the polylines from it. But since I don't want to import the osm data it is kinda annoying to delete them and then run the interpolation. Since the interpolation step takes quite some time it is very frustrating if you forgot this and wait that unused data is interpolated.

---
#### Here's what actually got changed :clap:
Allow the `pelias prepare interpolation` additional arguments which data should only be used (osm, oa, tiger). So you can skip parts where data is present but not used. You can also mix up (e.g.. `pelias prepare interpolation osm tiger`).

---
#### Here's how others can test the changes :eyes:
1.  Build the docker container for interpolation and run it.
2. Execute `pelias prepare interpolation oa` => only oa data should be interpolated


Reference PR: https://github.com/pelias/docker/pull/385
Closes #290

body:
This PR fixes the prodtest `bootloader-update` command and allows uploading a bootloader with the new PQC header on T3W1.

1) The `bootloader-update` command writes the new bootloader and boot header to the dedicated flash area (`BOOTUPDATE_AREA`). The update is finalized in the boardloader, so a `reboot` command is required after a successful upload.

2) The `bld_update.py` script was updated to avoid compressing the binary by default.

body:
### 🍀 Description
**Version:** `v1.1.0`
**Related:** #16 

<!--
Here you can describe changes and provide examples
-->
As mentioned in related issue:
> ... compiler may need to automatically link C libraries with included Deen file ...

In this PR it was implemented by doing same things as in `include` tool. But linking external C file does NOT provides its functions! **You still have to declare them by `extern` keyword!**

Example:
`test.c`
```
#include <stdio.h>

void greet(char *name) {
  printf("Hello, %s!\n", name);
}
```
`main.dn`
```deen
_link_c "test.c"
extern "C" fn greet(*char);

fn main {
  greet("mealet");
}
```

_Output:_
> Hello, mealet!

## Description

Updated some values in the outdated build.gradle of the plugin.
The example was updated to match it.

##
* Updated compileSdk to 34.  

The plugin is still at compileSdk 29.
34 is currently the minimum for a project to publish on the Play Store, and that is soon to be 35.

Some errors (like #845, #870) are directly caused by this low sdk.

##
* Updated Java 8 to 11

Unity 2021.3 and 2022.3  [both use Java 11](https://docs.unity3d.com/2022.3/Documentation/Manual/android-supported-dependency-versions.html).

And i'm also getting console warnings about Java 8 like:
```
warning: [options] source value 8 is obsolete and will be removed in a future release
warning: [options] target value 8 is obsolete and will be removed in a future release
warning: [options] To suppress warnings about obsolete options, use -Xlint:-options.
```

I can still make a release build with the plugin at Java 11 and my Flutter project at Java 8.  So this is (partially?) backwards compatible.

##

I updated the kotling and AGP version to be somewhat in line with these changes.  
These don't seem to matter much as Flutter projects on much newer Kotlin or AGP versions never show any warnings or errors related to them.
Just to be safe, I kept AGP below 8.

### Problem (investigation for nvbug 5224766) ```bash python thunder/benchmarks/benchmark_peft.py --model google/gemma-2-9b-it --trust-remote-code --attn-implementation sdpa --max-steps 10 --mbs 1 --seq-length 128 --compile thunder --fixed-num-hidden-layers 2 ``` failed with ```py RuntimeError: Failed to compute the min-cut on the graph due to a path with infinite capacity.Please report this error along with your function and relevant details at: https://github.com/Lightning-AI/lightning-thunder/issues/new ``` ### Analysis the reason is in the mincut, the source and sink sets have the same tensor which is illegal (`'t2081'`) ```py (Pdb) p required_consumer_vars ('t2075', 't1977', 't1998', 't2002', 't2968', 't2970', 't2973', 'l_self_modules_model_modules_layers_modules_1_modules_post_attention_layernorm_parameters_weight_', 't2045', 't2014', 't2975', 'l_self_modules_model_modules_layers_modules_1_modules_pre_feedforward_layernorm_parameters_weight_', 't1569', 't2112', 't2297', 't2285', 't2292', 't2609', 't2608', 't2156', 't2610', 't2151', 't2611', 't2058', 't2629', 't2628', 't2061', 't2050', 't2017', 't2630', 't2063', 't2054', 't2144', 't2631', 't2066', 't2633', 't2632', 't2070', 't2634', 't2125', 't2076', 't2073', 't2635', 't2128', 't2079', 't2139', 't2130', 't2081', 't2135', 't2084', 't2124', 't2119', 't2120', 't2115', 't2114', 't2116', 't2105', 't2101', 't2102', 't2097', 't2098', 't2091', 't2090', 't2117', 't2092', 't2123', 't2636', 't2086', 't2638', 't2637', 't2639', 't2640', 't2083', 't2078', 't2072', 't2068', 't2057', 't2052', 't2053', 't2048', 't2047', 't2049', 't2038', 't2034', 't2035', 't2030', 't2031', 't2024', 't2023', 't2025', 't2056', 't2641', 't2019', 't2016', 't2007', 't2001', 't2011', 't2002', 't1998', 't1977', 't2075') # overlap 't2081' ``` How we pick the source and sink: the source tensors: 1.inputs of the producer, 2.outputs of producer that are used by other consumers, the sink tensors: 1.output of the consumer, 2.the consumer's inputs `c_in` that are produced by other producers, 3.the output of the subsymbols along the path from `c_in` to their outputs in consumer In this case `t2081` comes from the the 1st in source tensors and the 3rd in sink tensors. The current graph structure does not ensure that source and sink tensors are disjoint. ### Proposal This PR adds a check to detect overlaps between source and sink tensors.
